package_info.package_manager: custom/none (deployed via exploitation, not a package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: The deployed web shell is a backdoor that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands, manipulate user accounts, enumerate and exfiltrate files, and maintain persistence on compromised MOVEit Transfer servers. It is installed post-exploitation via a critical SQL injection vulnerability (CVE-2023-34362) and is used for data theft and further compromise.

execution_context.file_location: deployed web shell file (arbitrary upload location on MOVEit Transfer web server)

malicious_snippets.code_language: javascript (or ASP.NET, depending on MOVEit deployment)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a specially crafted HTTP request with the correct password and X-siLock-Step1: -2 is received, the code deletes any users named 'Health Check Service' from the database, removing service accounts.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Deleting service accounts via a hidden web shell is a clear sign of malicious intent, as it disrupts legitimate monitoring and can help attackers evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal web applications do not provide undocumented HTTP header-based commands to delete privileged accounts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Administrative APIs may allow account deletion, but always with authentication, logging, and user interface—not hidden headers.

execution_context.file_location: deployed web shell file (arbitrary upload location on MOVEit Transfer web server)

malicious_snippets.code_language: javascript (or ASP.NET, depending on MOVEit deployment)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a specially crafted HTTP request with the correct password and X-siLock-Step1: -1 is received, the code enumerates all files in the database, including metadata such as file id, name, size, location, owner, and institution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Enumerating all files and metadata via a hidden backdoor is a classic reconnaissance and data theft technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate file listing is only available to authenticated, authorized users through official interfaces.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: File listing APIs exist, but are always authenticated and logged.

execution_context.file_location: deployed web shell file (arbitrary upload location on MOVEit Transfer web server)

malicious_snippets.code_language: javascript (or ASP.NET, depending on MOVEit deployment)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a specially crafted HTTP request with the correct password and an integer X-siLock-Step1 (not -1 or -2) is received, the code creates a new service account with a random username for the specified institution and adds it to the active sessions list.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Creating new privileged accounts via a hidden backdoor enables persistent access and lateral movement.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Account creation should only occur through official, logged, and authenticated administrative actions.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated account creation for onboarding, but never via hidden web shell.

execution_context.file_location: deployed web shell file (arbitrary upload location on MOVEit Transfer web server)

malicious_snippets.code_language: javascript (or ASP.NET, depending on MOVEit deployment)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a specially crafted HTTP request with the correct password and X-siLock-Step1, X-siLock-Step2, and X-siLock-Step3 headers is received, the code downloads the specified file from the MOVEit database, enabling arbitrary file exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Arbitrary file download via a hidden backdoor is a direct data exfiltration mechanism.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: File downloads should be strictly controlled, authenticated, and logged.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Official file download APIs, but never via undocumented headers.

attack_chain.action: Exploit SQL injection vulnerability (CVE-2023-34362) to gain unauthenticated access and upload the web shell backdoor.
attack_chain.leads_to: Web shell backdoor is deployed on the server.

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends HTTP requests with custom headers to authenticate to the web shell using the X-siLock-Comment password.
Attacker issues commands to delete service accounts, enumerate files, create new accounts, and download arbitrary files.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data exfiltration, persistence, and anti-forensics actions.

behavioral_signatures: HTTP requests to MOVEit Transfer endpoints with unusual or undocumented headers (e.g., X-siLock-Comment, X-siLock-Step1, etc.)
Creation or deletion of service accounts named 'Health Check Service' or with random 16-character names
Bulk file enumeration and metadata access outside normal user activity
Arbitrary file downloads initiated via web shell endpoints

Unexpected files in MOVEit Transfer web server directories
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP requests with X-siLock-Comment and related headers
Outbound connections or file downloads not matching normal MOVEit Transfer usage
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for HTTP requests to MOVEit Transfer servers containing undocumented headers such as X-siLock-Comment, X-siLock-Step1, X-siLock-Step2, and X-siLock-Step3. Alert on the creation or deletion of service accounts named 'Health Check Service' or with random names. Scan for known web shell file hashes and unexpected files in web server directories. Review logs for bulk file enumeration or download activity outside normal user patterns.
